title: Pantanal Wetland Hydrological Flux 2024
headline: Severe drought contracted wetland surface water extent by 64.2% across critical biomes.
story: The Pantanal is the world's largest tropical wetland. In 2024, prolonged South American drought and record heat led to a historic failure of the seasonal flood pulse, leaving vast lagoons desiccated and vulnerable to runaway wildfires. L-band SAR backscatter reveals severe water surface retraction and soil moisture depletion across vital aquatic refugia.
why_sar: Why radar sees through cloud and night: Dense wildfire smoke plumes blanketed the Pantanal during the dry season, but radar microwaves easily penetrated the smoke to track vanishing water holes.

story_steps.title: April Hydrological Baseline
story_steps.description: Expansive flooded marshes and dendritic channels sustained wetland biodiversity.

story_steps.title: August Extreme Desiccation
story_steps.description: Extreme drought evaporated lagoons, exposing dry mudflats and dry grass savannahs.

story_steps.title: Wetland Loss Vectorization
story_steps.description: Change detection polygons highlight critical dried water bodies and fragmented river oxbows.

story_steps.title: Ecological Fire Risk Vulnerability
story_steps.description: Dry peat and desiccated reed beds mapped by radar coincided with subsequent catastrophic wildfire ignitions.
